factors: Eight material claims including operator-only measurements
Consequential source-control, permission and recovery design
complexity.rationale: The technical and governance implications require a mapped argument, credible alternatives, explicit measurement limits and a falsifiable migration test.

sourceMap.rationale: This section distinguishes reported growth and attempted mitigations from measured traffic or a universal Git limitation.
This section separates the stated architecture from the proposed integrity, availability, IAM and recovery tests.
This section attributes performance to the operator and limits the human-review statement to source-control system changes.

sourceCoverage.rationale: The public source has no video timeline. Three distinct analytical sections are tied to checked original article headings and seven material source claims; the proposed test is original synthesis.

supportingArgument.rationale: Anthropic’s reported scale, online changeset design, cache structure and relative performance case are represented as operator claims with their strongest technical rationale.

evidenceRoles.rationale: The Reader distinguishes first-party workload and performance reports, primary documentation of alternatives, GhostMesh threat-model inference and an unrun experiment.

counterargument.rationale: Git partial clone and maintenance form a practical baseline, while the strongest opposing view is that Anthropic’s agent-heavy checkout volume could justify a server-centered system.

tradeoffs.rationale: The essay examines client simplicity against online availability, centralized authority, derived-metadata integrity, credential blast radius and recovery dependence.

falsifiability.rationale: A matched synthetic replay and outage, corruption, review and recovery drills could change the recommendation in either direction; no benchmark is presented as already run.

originalSynthesis.rationale: GhostMesh connects merge throughput to the separate human and machine authority needed for acceptance, deployment and rollback; the commit itself is not the final control.

performance.rationale: The essay contrasts reported relative checkout and CPU gains with missing percentile latency, reliability, matched tuned-Git workloads and accepted-change quality.

economics.rationale: The essay notes missing dollar costs and non-portable team staffing, and proposes CPU, network and operating cost per accepted change under matched workloads.

threatGovernance.rationale: The analysis names source bytes, derived metadata, agent authority, review authority and deployment authority, with explicit tests for failure and privilege boundaries.

decisionRationale: Tony qualitatively accepted the exact authored article SHA-256 4a5b455ef28b824e75c9dc521767f5813e42ee04ccca3b3f194fde942b0d7462 after reviewing the preview.
